records.wording: Marcionite reading adopted (retroversion): "coming from the heavens with great power" for NA27 "coming in a cloud with power and great glory". Tertullian quotes the verse as the Lord's words ("Post haec quid dominus?", 4.39.10) and repeats "coming from the heavens" (4.39.11); Roth: "from the heavens" very likely, "with power… great" secure, "and glory likely not present". His Latin "cum plurima virtute" cannot render NA27's two nouns. The cloud he brings in himself, from Daniel 7:13, as a separate text. NA27 apparatus: καὶ δυνάμει πολλῇ καὶ δόξῃ D e (sys.c).

witnesses.evidence: "Cum autem haec fient, erigetis vos, et levabitis capita, quoniam appropinquavit redemptio vestra".

records.wording: NA27. Tertullian lacks "your" with "heads"; Roth: likely not present, because Tertullian has "capita vestra" when he cites the verse in Res. 22.6, and D d omit the pronoun (Roth n. 434; not in the NA27 apparatus). Latin can leave the possessive unexpressed, so his "capita" can render NA27 (METHOD §5.4). Printed.
